[pricing: https://greenandfortune.co.uk/newsfeed/green-fortune-celebrates-double-shortlisting-at-the-cateys-2026] Skip to main content What We Do How We Do It Who We Are Why We Do It News & Views Get in Touch Restaurants, Bars & Cafés Workplace Dining Venues & Events Our Locations Green & Fortune Celebrates Double Shortlisting at The Cateys 2026 At Green & Fortune, creating memorable experiences has always been at the heart of what we do. From exceptional food and warm hospitality to meaningful community impact, our teams work every day to deliver moments that bring people together. That’s why we’re incredibly proud to announce that Green & Fortune has been shortlisted for two prestigious awards at the Cateys 2026. These nominations are a celebration not only of individual achievement, but of the people, partnerships and purpose that define Green & Fortune as an award-winning hospitality company who recently became B Corp certified. Charity Fundraising Shortlisted for the ‘This is Hospitality’ Award We are equally honoured to have been shortlisted for the “This is Hospitality” Award for our annual St Patrick’s Day Celebration, an event that has become one of the most important and meaningful dates in our calendar. More than just an event, this event is a celebration of community, generosity and the spirit of hospitality. Each year, our entire team comes together alongside clients, partners and friends of the business to raise vital funds for Hospitality Action and London Irish Centre. The impact of these charities is significant. Hospitality Action provides essential support to people working within our industry during times of hardship, while the London Irish Centre continues its vital work supporting the Irish community across the capital. Supporting both organisations is something incredibly close to our hearts. Since the event began, the St Patrick’s Lunch has raised an outstanding £355,000, with this year marking our biggest fundraising total yet. The continued support from our guests, suppliers, partners and team members is what makes this possible year after year. The nomination for the ‘This is Hospitality’ Award is especially meaningful because it recognises the values at the core of award-winning hospitality; bringing people together, supporting communities and making a positive difference beyond the dining table. We Need Your Support Unlike many awards, the “This is Hospitality” category is decided by public vote and we would be incredibly grateful for your support. If you’ve attended the St Patrick’s Lunch, worked with our team, supported our fundraising efforts or simply believe in the importance of community within hospitality, we would love your vote. Please vote for Green & Fortune here: Vote for Green & Fortune at The Cateys 2026 Every vote means a huge amount to our team and helps shine a spotlight on the power of hospitality creating meaningful change. [blog: https://greenandfortune.co.uk/newsfeed/london-museum] Skip to main content What We Do How We Do It Who We Are Why We Do It News & Views Get in Touch Restaurants, Bars & Cafés Workplace Dining Venues & Events Our Locations London Museum and Green & Fortune Set to Open Four Major New Food and Drink Destinations in Smithfield this November Four new distinct food and drink destinations are launching alongside London Museum’s opening at its new Smithfield site on 28th November 2026 Green & Fortune will work in partnership with Robin Gill as Food Curator, collaborating with Chef Director Dan Rampat on the culinary direction across all four venues New openings include flagship restaurant, Clerks House at London Museum, Bartholomew’s bar, the Temperance Cocoa Rooms café and The Roost, an incubator space with a rotating residency of London’s up and coming talent. Green & Fortune will collaborate with Mr Lyan Studio, working alongside Head of Beverage Joe Boxall on the Bartholomew’s drinks proposition, inspired by London Museum’s permanent galleries and temporary exhibitions. Dining and drinking at London Museum is set to represent the capital’s food scene, ensuring food and drink is a key component of the museum experience. Green & Fortune and London Museum have announced the launch of four major hospitality concepts at the museum’s new landmark Smithfield home, opening on 28th November 2026. Food curator Robin Gill will oversee the culinary direction across all four concepts alongside Green & Fortune Chef Director, Dan Rampat, including Clerks House at London Museum, a new all-day dining room; Bartholomew’s, a bar featuring a London inspired beverage programme with cocktails by Mr Lyan Studio; the Temperance Cocoa Rooms, a café open daily with extended 24 hour opening from Thursday to Sunday; and The Roost, a rotating residency space dedicated to showcasing some of the city’s most exciting talent. Green & Fortune’s Chief Executive, John Nugent comments “The ambition of London Museum will be matched by a hospitality offering and programme unseen in London. The Green & Fortune team, together with our collaborators, Robin Gill and Mr Lyan Studio will collectively create authentic London food and drink experiences for both museum visitors and Londoners alike. Making food and drink, not just part of the experience, but a reason to visit. We are a proud, deep rooted London business and are embracing the opportunity to develop a selection of new and refreshingly different locations in the museum, that will shift the dial in what galleries and museums offer. It is a tremendously purposeful project, and we are proud to be playing our part in it. Over the coming months we will share more details about what people can expect, make sure to watch this space.” The opening of London Museum in Smithfield completes a decade-long restoration of the Victorian General Market, returning the disused historic building to public use for the first time in over three decades.
